Net income was impacted by transaction-related expenses ▪ Adjusted EBITDA increased 6% to a record $168 million; margin expanded 40 basis points to a record 10.2% ▪ Total and funded backlog increased 6% and 7%, respectively, both reaching record levels of $9.4 billion and $6.8 billion ▪ Signed a definitive purchase agreement and finalizing novation for the divestiture of the remote-location contracts; made measurable progress on the Critical Infrastructure joint venture program ▪ Narrowing and reiterating mid-point of fiscal year 2026 revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance ranges; reiterating operating cash flow guidance range Chantilly, VA – October 28, 2026, Parsons Corporation (NYSE: PSN) today announced financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026. CEO Commentary “We delivered a strong third quarter, exceeding our commitments with record adjusted EBITDA and adjusted EBITDA margin, and robust operating cash flow and bookings across both Federal Solutions and Critical Infrastructure. This performance highlights the resilience of our diversified portfolio and the strength of our differentiated solutions and products. Strong awards, record total and funded backlog, and a robust pipeline provide a solid foundation for continued organic growth,” said Carey Smith, chair, president, and chief executive officer. “We also continued to strengthen our portfolio, making meaningful progress on the strategic initiatives we outlined last quarter. While we continue to navigate procurement timing and geopolitical uncertainty, the alignment of our differentiated capabilities with our customers’ most critical national security and infrastructure needs reinforces our confidence in Parsons’ outlook. We remain focused on disciplined execution, converting our strong pipeline and recent awards into profitable growth, and delivering long-term value for our customers, employees, and shareholders.” Third Quarter 2026 Results Year-over-Year Comparisons (Q3 2026 vs. Q3 2025) Total revenue for the third quarter of 2026 increased by $29 million, or 2%, to $1.7 billion and was down 1% on an organic basis. Excluding the company's confidential contract, total revenue increased 5% and organic revenue increased 2%, driven by growth in our Cyber and Electronic Warfare and Transportation markets. Operating income decreased 4% to $104 million primarily due to higher transaction-related expenses. Net income decreased 16% to $54 parsons.com ©Parsons Corporation. Third Quarter 2026 Key Performance Indicators ▪ Book-to-bill ratio: 1.1x on net bookings of $1.8 billion. ▪ Book-to-bill ratio (trailing twelve months): 1.1x on net bookings of $7.3 billion. ▪ Record total backlog of $9.4 billion, up $530 million, or 6%, from Q3 2025. Record funded backlog of $6.8 billion represented 73% of total backlog and increased 7% year-over-year. ▪ Cash flow from operating activities: Q3 2026 of $269 million compared to $16 3 million in third quarter of 2025. On a trailing-12-month basis, the company generated $490 million in operating cash flow, an increase of 12% over the prior 12-month period. parsons.com ©Parsons Corporation. All Rights Reserved. 4 Significant Contract Wins Parsons continues to win new business across both segments. During the third quarter of 2026, the company received three contract actions valued at more than $100 million each and continued to expand its use of Other Transaction Agreements (OTAs). ▪ Received an increase in the ceiling value of the five-year, sole-source OTA with U.S. Cyber Command to $750 million. Under this agreement, the company has begun full-rate production of the Joint Cyber Hunt Kit, or JCHK. In total, the company has booked $250 million on this agreement. ▪ Awarded a 66-month, $495 million ceiling value contract for a national security customer to acquire and deploy advanced communications, power, and software capabilities. The company booked $37 million on this contract during the third quarter. ▪ Booked $234 million of the $514 million Missile Defense Agency’s (MDA) Technical, Engineering, Advisory, and Management Support (TEAMS) – NEXT Systems Engineering contract two-year option period. For the first nine months of 2026, the company has booked $429 million on this contract extension. ▪ Awarded a five-year, $97 million Other Transaction Agreement by a government customer to deliver technology to simulate radio frequency and cyber conditions. The company booked $4 million on this agreement during the third quarter. ▪ Awarded a five-year, $95 million Other Transaction Agreement by a government customer to modernize software supporting early-warning capabilities. The company booked $19 million on this agreement during the third quarter. ▪ Awarded an OTA by the Department of War for solutions related to the Pacific Command theater of operations. This three-year OTA has a ceiling value of $95 million and expands the company’s footprint in PACOM, enabling continued deployment of exquisite solutions that advance mission success and protect national security. The company booked $30 million on this agreement during the third quarter. ▪ Awarded a 75-month, $86 million OTA by Army Contracting Command – Rock Island, in coordination with Air Force Civil Engineering Center. Under this agreement, which represents new work for the company, Parsons will serve as the Owner’s Advisor for the development of U.S. Space Command's new headquarters at Redstone Arsenal in Huntsville, Alabama, providing comprehensive program and construction management support during planning, design, construction, and operationalization. This OTA will oversee one of the Department of War’s largest progressive design-build initiatives to date and is one of the Air Force’s first uses of an Owner’s Advisor delivery approach. The company booked the full amount on this agreement during the third quarter. ▪ Awarded a $70 million single-award task order under the Air Base, Air Defense IDIQ contract. Under this task order, Parsons will support the integration, testing, deployment, sustainment, maintenance, and operational transition of point-defense systems designed to defend personnel, aircraft, installations, and other critical assets from emerging aerial threats through Europe and Africa. This contract has a four-year period of performance with three 12-month option periods. The company booked $46 million on this contract during the third quarter. CFO Transition Matt Ofilos, Parsons’ Chief Financial Officer, has notified the Company of his decision to resign from his position, effective November 6, 2026, to pursue another professional opportunity. Mr. Ofilos’ resignation is not the result of any disagreement with the Company on any matter relating to the Company’s operations, policies, or practices. George Ball, who served as Parsons’ Chief Financial Officer from 2008 to 2022 and has served on the Company’s Board of Directors since 2022, has been appointed interim Chief Financial Officer, effective November 6, 2026. parsons.com ©Parsons Corporation. Parsons was also designated a Best Veteran Employer. ▪ Received an Award of Merit under the Highway/Bridge category for the Brooklyn Bridge Rehabilitation project by Engineering News-Record (ENR) New York. This project was also honored with the Centennial Project of the Year by the New York State Society of Professional Engineers. ▪ Recognized by ENR Midwest with an Award of Merit under the Highway/Bridge category for the I-70 Rocheport Bridge Replacement Design-Build and Best Project designation for The Gordie Howe International Bridge Project, which was also named a Finalist in the Midwest Best Projects of the Year by ENR. ▪ Honored with the Best Project designation under the Airport/Transit category, Award of Merit for Excellence in Sustainability, and Excellence in Safety for the Federal Way Link Extension project by ENR Northwest. ▪ Awarded Digital Transformation of the Year under the Consultant category at the Construction Technology Awards 2026. ▪ Recognized as a Best Veteran Employer by Vetted Employer for 2026-2027. This official designation was earned by meeting the benchmark requirements of the Vetted Checkup Survey, which evaluates an organization’s veteran hiring practices, retention, and military-connected support programs.
